name: Task
description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. The agent starts with no context from this conversation, so your prompt must be self-contained — include file paths, line numbers, and what specifically to change.

Agents are useful for parallelizing independent queries or protecting the main context window from large result sets.

## When to use

Brief the agent like a smart colleague who just walked into the room — it hasn't seen this conversation, doesn't know what you've tried, doesn't understand why this task matters.
- Explain what you're trying to accomplish and why.
- Describe what you've already learned or ruled out.
- Give enough context about the surrounding problem that the agent can make judgment calls rather than just following a narrow instruction.
- If you need a short response, say so ("report in under 200 words").
- Lookups: hand over the exact command. Investigations: hand over the question.

Terse command-style prompts produce shallow, generic work. Never delegate understanding — write prompts that prove you understood: include file paths, line numbers, what specifically to change.

## When not to use

If the target is already known, use the direct tool: Read for a known path, Grep for a specific symbol or string. Reserve Task for open-ended questions that span the codebase.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task. Defaults to general-purpose when no subagents are configured.
